stem: A school-aged child presents with facial swelling and a halo around the opening of the parotid gland in the buccal mucosa; which diagnosis best matches this finding?
explanation: Mumps is the correct diagnosis because parotid swelling with a halo around the parotid duct opening in the buccal mucosa is a characteristic oral finding.

rationale: A halo around the parotid duct opening points to parotid gland involvement, which is most consistent with mumps.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because dental facial cellulitis can cause facial swelling, but it does not characteristically produce a halo around the parotid duct opening.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because mumps commonly causes parotid gland swelling and can produce a halo around the opening of the parotid duct in the buccal mucosa.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because aphthous ulceration causes painful mucosal ulcers rather than parotid swelling or a duct-opening halo.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a mucocoele from lip-biting usually presents as a bluish swelling on the lower lip, not at the parotid duct opening.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because herpetic gingivostomatitis causes diffuse painful gingival and oral lesions, not the parotid-duct halo described here.
